concept: participant recruitment for a post-stroke gait rehabilitation study using a wearable robotic exoskeleton

children.description: Specify stroke type, lesion characteristics, chronicity, and relevant demographic boundaries for the intended study population.
children.name: Define the target stroke population

children.description: Establish minimum and maximum requirements for walking ability, gait impairment, assistive-device use, and functional mobility.
children.name: Set gait-related inclusion criteria

children.description: Identify physical, biomechanical, and motor-control characteristics required for safe and effective use of the wearable robotic exoskeleton.
children.name: Specify exoskeleton suitability criteria

children.description: Specify unstable or high-risk cardiovascular conditions that make participation unsafe, such as recent major cardiac events, uncontrolled arrhythmias, decompensated heart failure, or unstable angina.
children.name: Define cardiovascular exclusion criteria

children.description: Collect relevant cardiovascular history, including prior myocardial infarction, heart failure, arrhythmias, vascular disease, syncope, and recent hospitalizations.
children.name: Review medical history and current diagnoses

children.description: Ask about chest pain, exertional dyspnea, palpitations, dizziness, fainting, unusual fatigue, and other symptoms suggesting cardiovascular instability.
children.name: Verify current cardiovascular symptoms

children.description: Identify and gather all devices needed for recruitment screening and baseline gait assessments, including the exoskeleton, motion sensors, force-measurement tools, timing devices, and safety equipment.
children.name: Inventory required equipment

children.description: Check each device for visible damage, wear, loose components, depleted batteries, software faults, or other issues that could affect participant safety or measurement quality.
children.name: Inspect equipment condition

children.description: Verify the exact wearable robotic exoskeleton, available sizes, modular components, and study-specific configuration intended for participant use.
children.name: Confirm exoskeleton model and configuration

children.description: Assess whether the device can accommodate the expected range of post-stroke body dimensions, limb lengths, joint limitations, and asymmetries.
children.name: Check participant fit and adjustability

children.description: Confirm operation of emergency stops, joint-limit protections, torque limits, harnesses, fall-prevention supports, and other safeguards required during gait rehabilitation.
children.name: Validate clinical safety features

children.description: Check that onboard sensors and any supplementary wearable or laboratory systems can capture the gait, mobility, and intervention data required by the study.
children.name: Confirm sensing and data-capture compatibility

children.description: Verify compatibility with available walking surfaces, parallel bars, treadmills, ramps, charging facilities, network access, and clinical monitoring equipment.
children.name: Test interoperability with clinical facilities

children.description: Run representative setup, fitting, walking, monitoring, data transfer, charging, and fault-recovery procedures before recruiting participants for device-based sessions.
children.name: Complete end-to-end system testing

children.description: Confirm that the exoskeleton model, control unit, sensors, workstation, and operating system meet the validated firmware and software requirements.
children.name: Verify hardware and system compatibility

children.description: Retrieve the authorized firmware, drivers, control application, and supporting files from the validated source using the study-approved versions.
children.name: Obtain approved software packages

children.description: Document the device make, model, serial number, and hardware revision used during recruitment-related assessments.
children.name: Identify the exoskeleton model and hardware revision

children.description: Record participant-specific frame dimensions, joint alignment adjustments, cuff positions, and other fitting parameters.
children.name: Document mechanical fit and adjustment settings

children.description: Document torque or force assistance, gait-phase settings, control mode, impedance parameters, and related robotic support configurations.
children.name: Record assistance and control parameters

children.description: List the sensors enabled, their placement, calibration status, sampling settings, and any calibration procedure used.
children.name: Capture sensor and calibration configuration

children.description: Record speed limits, range-of-motion limits, emergency-stop configuration, harness settings, and other safety-critical parameters.
children.name: Log safety and operational settings

children.description: Track configuration changes by date, participant, operator, reason, and approval status so recruitment and screening records remain reproducible.
children.name: Maintain configuration change history

children.description: Document software versions, firmware revisions, device identifiers, installation dates, and configuration settings for traceability.
children.name: Record version and configuration information

children.description: Install the required drivers, runtime components, communication libraries, and security certificates needed for the exoskeleton software to operate.
children.name: Install device drivers and dependencies

children.description: Apply the validated firmware to the wearable robotic exoskeleton according to the manufacturer’s controlled update procedure.
children.name: Update the exoskeleton firmware

children.description: Confirm successful communication, sensor detection, calibration access, error handling, and safe startup through documented functional checks before participant use.
children.name: Run post-installation verification

children.description: Ensure the exoskeleton, sensors, data-acquisition systems, and analysis interfaces use the study-approved firmware and software versions.
children.name: Install validated firmware and software

children.description: Perform the manufacturer-approved calibration procedures for inertial sensors, pressure sensors, force plates, cameras, or other systems used to quantify walking performance.
children.name: Calibrate motion and gait sensors

children.description: Verify joint-angle sensing, actuator output, assistance settings, alignment references, and emergency-stop functionality before using the device with prospective participants.
children.name: Calibrate the robotic exoskeleton

children.description: Prepare adjustable device dimensions, sensor placement references, body-size inputs, walking speed limits, and recording parameters for the anticipated post-stroke participant population.
children.name: Configure participant-specific measurement settings

children.description: Run an end-to-end test using a known movement or test subject to confirm synchronized data capture, correct file labeling, adequate storage, emergency procedures, and reliable equipment operation.
children.name: Verify recording and safety readiness

children.description: Verify that blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, thermometers, and heart-rate monitors are functional, appropriately sized, and within calibration requirements.
children.name: Prepare calibrated measurement equipment

children.description: Have the participant rest, avoid recent exertion when feasible, and remain seated or positioned safely before measurements begin.
children.name: Confirm participant readiness

children.description: Specify the calendar dates, daily time range, and duration during which participant assessments will occur.
children.name: Define the measurement window

children.description: Determine when the standardized period begins after screening, consent, and baseline eligibility confirmation.
children.name: Set measurement timing relative to enrollment

children.description: Collect availability constraints and identify appointment slots that participants can reliably attend.
children.name: Coordinate participant availability

children.description: Specify the space, accessibility, safety, equipment, and staffing requirements for participant screening and gait assessments.
children.name: Define facility requirements

children.description: Locate rehabilitation clinics, hospitals, laboratories, or community sites that can accommodate post-stroke participants and exoskeleton assessments.
children.name: Identify suitable facilities

children.description: Confirm wheelchair access, accessible entrances and restrooms, parking or public transport options, and practical arrival procedures.
children.name: Verify accessibility and transport

children.description: Check that the facility has sufficient floor area, walking paths, ceiling clearance, power access, and surfaces suitable for the wearable robotic exoskeleton.
children.name: Confirm exoskeleton compatibility

children.description: Obtain suitable dates and recurring time slots that support recruitment screening, baseline assessments, and participant appointment demand.
children.name: Schedule assessment availability

children.description: Coordinate emergency response, fall-management, infection-control, equipment-storage, and participant supervision procedures with facility personnel.
children.name: Establish facility safety procedures

children.description: Document room bookings, access permissions, costs, cancellation terms, responsible contacts, and operational arrangements before recruitment begins.
children.name: Finalize reservation agreements

children.description: Book the gait laboratory, rehabilitation space, or clinical area needed for standardized measurements.
children.name: Reserve assessment facilities

children.description: Specify which staff members will conduct screening, consent discussions, eligibility assessments, gait evaluations, and recruitment documentation.
children.name: Define staff roles and responsibilities

children.description: Select clinicians or research staff with relevant expertise in post-stroke rehabilitation, neurological assessment, and participant-facing research procedures.
children.name: Identify qualified assessment personnel

children.description: Confirm staff competency in human-subjects protection, informed consent, post-stroke safety, mobility assistance, and study-specific procedures.
children.name: Verify required credentials and training

children.description: Prepare staff to recognize contraindications, assist with device fitting and walking trials, manage falls or adverse events, and follow emergency procedures.
children.name: Train staff on exoskeleton-related safety

children.description: Use approved scripts, checklists, forms, and operating procedures so recruitment assessments are delivered consistently across staff and participants.
children.name: Standardize screening and assessment procedures

children.description: Evaluate staff through supervised practice, demonstrations, or mock assessments and retain records showing authorization to conduct recruitment and screening activities.
children.name: Assess and document staff competency

children.description: Schedule qualified personnel to administer the same measurement procedures across all recruited participants.
children.name: Assign trained assessment staff

children.description: Specify the exact wearable robotic exoskeleton, controller, attachments, and software configuration required for participant assessments and study sessions.
children.name: Confirm exoskeleton model and configuration

children.description: Secure ownership, rental, loan, or manufacturer-supplied access to the exoskeleton and all required accessories for the recruitment period.
children.name: Verify equipment procurement or loan arrangements

children.description: Reserve the exoskeleton, charging facilities, treatment space, and supporting equipment for screening, fitting, demonstrations, and enrollment visits.
children.name: Schedule equipment access

children.description: Check mechanical components, batteries, sensors, straps, footwear interfaces, and safety features to ensure the equipment is operational before participant contact.
children.name: Inspect equipment condition

children.description: Install approved software, configure study settings, calibrate sensors, and confirm that data recording and export functions work correctly.
children.name: Complete calibration and software setup

children.description: Organize measurement tools, adjustable components, hygiene materials, replacement straps, and other supplies needed to fit the exoskeleton to different participants.
children.name: Prepare participant sizing and fitting supplies

children.description: Define procedures for routine servicing, battery replacement, technical support, equipment failure, and backup access so recruitment activities are not disrupted.
children.name: Establish maintenance and contingency coverage

children.description: Ensure the wearable robotic exoskeleton, gait sensors, calibration tools, and recording systems are available during each appointment.
children.name: Arrange equipment availability

children.description: Contact each eligible participant to verify the agreed appointment date and time still work.
children.name: Reconfirm participant availability

children.description: Book screening, baseline assessment, training, intervention, and follow-up visits according to the study protocol.
children.name: Schedule required study visits

children.description: Determine how participants will travel to the research site and arrange approved transportation support when needed.
children.name: Coordinate transportation arrangements

children.description: Confirm whether a caregiver or support person must attend visits and record their availability.
children.name: Verify caregiver or companion attendance

children.description: Send information about the site address, entrance, parking, check-in location, accessibility features, and arrival time.
children.name: Provide arrival and access instructions

children.description: Tell participants what to bring or wear, including mobility aids, medication information, comfortable clothing, and suitable footwear.
children.name: Prepare visit-specific requirements

children.description: Record appointment confirmations, reminders, cancellations, rescheduling needs, transportation issues, and other logistical updates in the recruitment system.
children.name: Document confirmations and changes

children.description: Send participants finalized appointment details, preparation instructions, transportation information, and procedures for reporting delays or cancellations.
children.name: Confirm appointments and logistics

children.description: Measure resting heart rate at a consistent time and under comparable pre-assessment conditions for every candidate.
children.name: Schedule a standardized measurement period

children.description: Have the candidate sit or recline quietly and avoid recent exertion, caffeine, nicotine, or other factors that may temporarily alter heart rate.
children.name: Prepare the participant for rest

children.description: Specify which gait, mobility, safety, and participant-characteristic outcomes the device must measure during recruitment screening and study assessments.
children.name: Define measurement objectives

children.description: Establish requirements for accuracy, reliability, wearability, compatibility with post-stroke mobility limitations, and use alongside the wearable robotic exoskeleton.
children.name: Set device selection criteria

children.description: Establish recruitment-relevant criteria such as intended users, assistance modes, mobility requirements, fitting constraints, safety features, and study compatibility.
children.name: Define device comparison criteria

children.description: Compile wearable robotic exoskeleton models that are available, investigational, or accessible through collaborating clinics and research institutions.
children.name: Inventory candidate exoskeletons

children.description: Assess whether each device supports the gait impairments, assistance needs, body dimensions, functional levels, and medical profiles represented in the target participant population.
children.name: Verify post-stroke suitability

children.description: Determine how each device's requirements affect inclusion and exclusion criteria, including strength, balance, range of motion, cognitive capacity, and walking ability.
children.name: Review eligibility implications

children.description: Compare device-specific risks, contraindications, supervision needs, emergency procedures, and screening information required before enrollment.
children.name: Assess participant safety requirements

children.description: Estimate the size and accessibility of the eligible participant pool based on device availability, fitting limitations, training demands, clinic infrastructure, and geographic reach.
children.name: Evaluate recruitment feasibility

children.description: Evaluate available measurement devices against the predefined technical, clinical, usability, and study-operational requirements.
children.name: Compare candidate devices

children.description: Verify that the exoskeleton is designed and cleared for individuals with post-stroke gait impairments matching the study population.
children.name: Confirm intended-use population

children.description: Confirm fit ranges, adjustment mechanisms, and compatibility with participants’ body sizes and limb proportions.
children.name: Check device dimensions and adjustability

children.description: Verify device weight, maximum supported body weight, and any limb-loading or joint-loading restrictions relevant to screening.
children.name: Review weight and physical-load limits

children.description: Confirm supported walking modes, assistance levels, speed ranges, step parameters, and adaptability to post-stroke gait patterns.
children.name: Validate gait-assistance capabilities

children.description: Identify the minimum standing, stepping, balance, strength, and walking abilities required for safe device operation.
children.name: Confirm mobility and balance requirements

children.description: Verify harness requirements, fall protection, emergency stop functions, monitoring systems, alarms, and safe shutdown procedures.
children.name: Review safety and emergency features

children.description: Confirm battery duration, setup time, required supervision, surface requirements, space needs, and restrictions affecting participant eligibility.
children.name: Check operational and environmental constraints

children.description: Inspect sensor configuration, sampling rate, battery life, data storage, connectivity, calibration procedures, and software compatibility.
children.name: Verify technical specifications

children.description: Check whether the device can be safely and comfortably applied to participants with hemiparesis, balance impairment, spasticity, or limited dexterity.
children.name: Assess participant usability

children.description: Confirm that the measurement device does not interfere with exoskeleton fitting, walking assistance, movement, safety systems, or therapist supervision.
children.name: Test device-exoskeleton integration

children.description: Conduct trial measurements, identify setup or data-quality problems, and document standardized procedures for device preparation, placement, operation, and inspection.
children.name: Pilot and document the measurement workflow

children.description: Use a validated heart-rate monitor or clinical vital-sign device and verify that it is functioning and appropriately positioned.
children.name: Select and inspect the measurement device

children.description: Specify how long participants should rest or acclimate before gait measurements begin.
children.name: Define the stabilization period

children.description: Set up a nearby chair, wheelchair, or supported standing device with adequate space, stability, and clear access.
children.name: Prepare an appropriate rest area

children.description: Tell potential participants that they may request seated or supported rest at any time during recruitment-related walking or demonstration activities.
children.name: Explain rest availability

children.description: Watch for signs such as slowing, loss of balance, shortness of breath, weakness, dizziness, or visible exertion that indicate a need to stop.
children.name: Monitor fatigue and instability

children.description: Invite the person to sit or use supported rest before fatigue becomes pronounced, especially after standing, walking, or equipment demonstrations.
children.name: Offer rest proactively

children.description: Provide appropriate staff assistance and mobility support when the person moves from standing or walking into a seated or supported position.
children.name: Assist with safe transitions

children.description: Ensure stable positioning, suitable posture, access to mobility aids, and sufficient time for recovery without pressure to continue.
children.name: Maintain comfort during rest

children.description: Record rest requests, observed fatigue, assistance required, recovery time, and any safety concerns relevant to recruitment eligibility or visit planning.
children.name: Document rest-related observations

children.description: Give participants sufficient time in a safe seated or supported position to reduce fatigue and physiological fluctuation.
children.name: Provide seated or supported rest

children.description: Allow participants to become comfortable with the device, its fit, and its operating sensations before assessment.
children.name: Acclimate participants to the exoskeleton

children.description: Adjust harnesses, straps, alignment, and assistance settings before the stabilization interval starts.
children.name: Complete initial device fitting

children.description: Ask participants about pain, dizziness, spasticity, exertion, and fatigue and postpone testing if recovery is incomplete.
children.name: Verify symptom and fatigue readiness

children.description: Use the same sequence of rest, device familiarization, safety checks, and readiness confirmation for every participant.
children.name: Standardize the pre-measurement routine

children.description: Wait until the candidate has remained still and relaxed long enough for heart rate to reach a stable resting level.
children.name: Allow stabilization before measurement

children.description: Repeat the measurement after additional rest when the value is unexpected, unstable, or potentially affected by device error.
children.name: Repeat or verify an abnormal reading

children.description: Record the heart rate, time, body position, device used, relevant pre-measurement conditions, and any symptoms or irregular rhythm observations.
children.name: Document the result and measurement conditions

children.description: Measure and document the participant’s resting pulse using a validated monitor or standardized manual method.
children.name: Record resting heart rate

children.description: Obtain and record blood pressure using the correct cuff size, arm position, and repeated readings when required by the protocol.
children.name: Measure resting blood pressure

children.description: Measure and document peripheral oxygen saturation with a properly positioned pulse oximeter.
children.name: Assess oxygen saturation

children.description: Obtain and record temperature using the study-approved method and device.
children.name: Measure body temperature

children.description: Compare vital signs with study thresholds, document measurement conditions and values, and escalate abnormal findings before recruitment or gait-testing procedures proceed.
children.name: Review and document safety findings

children.description: Record resting blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and rhythm when feasible, using predefined thresholds for repeat measurement or exclusion.
children.name: Measure baseline vital signs

children.description: Evaluate symptoms and vital-sign changes during safe, low-intensity movement or routine mobility to identify abnormal cardiovascular responses before exoskeleton training.
children.name: Assess response to basic activity

children.description: Document cardiovascular medications, adherence, recent dose changes, and treatments that may indicate unresolved instability or affect exercise safety.
children.name: Review medications and recent treatment changes

children.description: Refer candidates with concerning history, symptoms, abnormal measurements, or unclear risk to their physician or a qualified clinician for clearance before enrollment.
children.name: Obtain medical clearance when indicated

children.description: Exclude candidates with recent serious cardiac events, uncontrolled arrhythmias, unstable angina, or other cardiovascular conditions that make assisted walking unsafe.
children.name: Screen for unstable cardiovascular conditions

children.description: Exclude candidates with fractures, severe osteoporosis, unstable joints, major contractures, or other orthopedic conditions incompatible with exoskeleton loading.
children.name: Assess musculoskeletal load-bearing limitations

children.description: Check for open wounds, active ulcers, severe skin disease, or impaired tissue tolerance at areas contacting the device, including the pelvis, legs, and feet.
children.name: Evaluate skin and pressure-injury risk

children.description: Exclude candidates with uncontrolled seizures, rapidly worsening neurological disease, or impairments that could make robotic gait training medically unsafe.
children.name: Identify uncontrolled neurological conditions

children.description: Determine whether profound postural instability, frequent unexplained falls, or inability to follow supported standing procedures creates unacceptable injury risk.
children.name: Check for severe balance and fall-risk hazards

children.description: Identify implanted devices, active treatments, or medication-related risks that could interfere with exoskeleton operation, exertion tolerance, or safe gait training.
children.name: Review contraindicating medical devices or treatments

children.description: Exclude candidates with acute infection, fever, uncontrolled blood pressure, respiratory instability, or other unresolved conditions requiring medical stabilization before participation.
children.name: Confirm acute illness and vital-sign stability

children.description: Screen for cardiovascular, neurological, orthopedic, skin, pain, and other conditions that could make participation unsafe.
children.name: Define medical safety exclusions

children.description: Determine the capacity needed to understand instructions, provide informed consent, communicate discomfort, and follow the rehabilitation protocol.
children.name: Establish cognitive and communication requirements

children.description: Identify participant characteristics such as age, sex, affected side, impairment severity, and comorbidities for balanced enrollment or planned subgroup analysis.
children.name: Set demographic and clinical stratification factors

children.description: Translate all criteria into measurable screening questions, assessments, documentation requirements, and decision rules for consistent enrollment decisions.
children.name: Operationalize eligibility screening

children.description: The characteristics, clinical criteria, functional requirements, safety considerations, and exclusion factors that define the target participant population.
children.name: Participant eligibility and population definition

root.name: participant recruitment for a post-stroke gait rehabilitation study using a wearable robotic exoskeleton
